claims.statement: The `hypermnesic` CLI is an argparse surface: `build_parser()` builds the subcommand tree, each leaf sets `func`, and `main()` returns the int exit code produced by `args.func(args)` rather than calling `sys.exit`, which is what lets the test suite invoke `cli.main([...])` in-process. The console entry point is the `hypermnesic = "hypermnesic.cli:main"` script in pyproject.toml.

The parser registers exactly 22 top-level subcommands, grouped by role: `local-proof`; the projection builds `index`, `embed`, `reindex`, `init`, `converge`; the read verbs `retrieve`, `think`, `resolve`, `list-folders`; the write verbs `commit-note`, `capture`, `daily-review`; the `memory` group; the `clients` group; `install-hooks`; the `doctor`/`status` pair; and the serving/provisioning verbs `serve`, `serve-cloud`, `setup`, `install`.

`--version` prints the `__version__` value imported from `src/hypermnesic/__init__.py`, which is an in-package mirror and not the authority: `pyproject.toml [project].version` is, and `scripts/check_version_consistency.py` fails the build when the mirror or a manifest diverges from it.

Every index-reading CLI verb converges the index toward HEAD before serving, with a debounced default pass: `retrieve`, `resolve`, and `list-folders` expose `--now` to force a non-debounced pass (so a self-write committed inside the debounce window is visible in one command), while `think` takes the debounced default and has no `--now` flag.

`daily-review` is the exception among index readers: it does not converge, opening the index only when `<repo>/.hypermnesic/index.db` already exists and otherwise degrading to a files-and-audit-log review, and it emits its dashboard as a review-gated proposal branch rather than changing source notes.

The CLI's mutating verbs are preview-by-default behind a per-verb flag: `commit-note` is a read-only dry run unless `--commit` is passed, and `memory forget`, `memory revert`, and `clients revoke` are read-only previews unless `--apply` is passed. `capture` is the deliberate exception, committing raw text immediately into the `sources/` free-append zone.

`--json` is supported by 20 of the 22 subcommands and always renders through one helper, `_print_json`, which uses `json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`; the two exceptions are `serve` and `serve-cloud`, which run the server to completion and therefore never return.

Handled CLI failures print a one-line stderr message and return exit code 1 instead of a success shape — `local-proof`, `list-folders` with a bad `--root`, `serve` on a refused construction, `serve-cloud`, `setup`, `install`, every `memory` leaf, and `clients`. `commit-note` has no handler-level exception clause, so a guard refusal propagates as an exception and exits non-zero without that tidy stderr line.

The CLI splits graceful degradation from fail-loud by verb class: read verbs tolerate an absent or dead embedding credential and report `degraded_lexical_only` on the result, whereas the projection-build verbs (`index`, `embed`, `reindex`, `init`) call `embed.smoke_embed_or_die`, which proves the key is actually readable by the SDK and raises rather than silently indexing.

Five CLI verbs are deliberate twins of MCP tools and share their modules and result shapes: `retrieve`↔`search` (identical hit projection and convergence fields), `list-folders`↔`list_folders` (identical JSON key set), `think`↔`think`, `resolve`↔`resolve`, and `commit-note`↔`commit_note`.

The `commit-note` twin pair is intentionally asymmetric in its default: the CLI verb is a dry-run preview unless `--commit` is passed, while the MCP `commit_note` tool declares no preview parameter and always commits.

The `memory` and `clients` groups have no MCP counterpart — owner-facing control over files, git, audit entries, and secret-free OAuth grant metadata stays off the agent-facing wire; conversely `build_context`, `read_note`, and the `hypermnesic_search` alias are MCP-only with no CLI twin.

`list-folders` reuses the server's single write-surface coercion (`mcp_server._effective_write_surface`) instead of re-deriving writability, so the CLI's folder preview cannot disagree with the live MCP write surface.

Derived state is selected separately from the vault: read verbs, `embed`, `converge`, `memory`, and `daily-review` take `--index-db` (default `<repo>/.hypermnesic/index.db` via `index.state_dir_for`), `index`/`reindex` take `--state-dir` to keep state entirely outside the indexed repo, and the in-repo default state dir is added to `.git/info/exclude` so it never enters git.

`commit-note` and `capture` accept neither `--index-db` nor `--state-dir`: they open only the in-repo `<repo>/.hypermnesic/index.db`, and when it is absent they still commit and simply skip the index projection — the git write is the commitment and the index is catch-up work.

`serve` and `serve-cloud` require `--index-db` and accept an optional `--repo` that re-anchors the served vault, because omitting `--repo` makes the server derive the repo from the index-db grandparent — so a non-standard index location must be paired with `--repo` or dense credential lookup can point at an unrelated parent directory.

`capture` reaches git through the proposal queue's immutable free-append fast path: `capture.capture` calls `propose.propose` with `allowlist=["sources/"]`, and `propose` routes a new file in an immutable append zone straight to `commit_note` with no proposal branch, which is why no CLI verb calls `propose` for a curated write.

`doctor` and `status` are the same command: one loop registers both names against `_cmd_doctor`, which delegates to the non-mutating `doctor.run_doctor` (it writes no files, services, secrets, or commits, and an `--env-file` check never prints contents), so the alias cannot drift.

`install` is an offline, pure provisioning verb: it renders service artifacts, writes role config, and installs the convergence hook, then returns `manual_steps` for the host-specific actions (service enable/start, index build) instead of performing them, so the CLI provisions nothing by itself.

`local-proof` fails as a structured `LocalProofError` printed to stderr as `local-proof failed: …` plus a `next:` line with exit 1 and no traceback, and its JSON contract deliberately omits the absolute repo path so the output stays shareable.

Credential discipline holds across the CLI: keys come from the process environment or a gitignored repo-root `.env` and are never echoed, `serve-cloud` requires the operator approval token in the environment and never accepts it as a flag (a flag would leak through the process table / logs), and `doctor --env-file` is checked for existence and permissions only.

CLI `think` and CLI `resolve` do not carry the `manual_reindex_recommended` convergence field that their MCP twins append, so the twin pairs are not yet byte-identical and a change to either side must decide explicitly whether the gap stays.

`tests/test_cli.py` pins the surface's load-bearing behaviors: converge-before-serving for `retrieve` and `think`, the lexically degraded hit shape under a neutralized key, `--now` freshness against the debounce window, list-folders JSON parity with the MCP output shape, preview-by-default for `commit-note`, exit-1 refusals for serve/serve-cloud/setup/local-proof, and the absence of the retired `serve-auth`/`auth-add-client` subcommands.

A CLI-first agent host integrates through the CLI verbs themselves: `tests/test_hermes_plugin.py` pins that the Hermes plugin teaches exactly `retrieve`, `think`, `resolve`, `list-folders`, `capture`, and `commit-note`, making a rename of any of those a cross-surface change rather than a local edit.
